newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper replaces armed forces chief.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper replaces armed forces chief.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper replaced the head of Colombia's armed forces, Gen. Harold Bedoya, on Thursday after a series of increasingly public disagreements, citing only "reasons of state."

Bedoya, who was appointed at the end of last October amid one of the worst leftist guerrilla offensives in decades, made no immediate comment about his future plans but said last month that he would consider running for the presidency once he ended his military career.
Bedoya was replaced by army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, according to a statement read by Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri.

"The president decided today to introduce changes in the armed forces, taking into account reasons of state," the statement said. "The national government wants to publicly thank Bedoya who fulfilled an important task at the head of the armed forces."

In recent weeks, Bedoya and Samper issued sharply contradicting public statements about how to confront the country's main guerrilla armies whose nationwide offensive, which began last August, has continued virtually unabated.

Bedoya, who has been accused of serious human rights violations by domestic and international human rights groups, firmly rejected Samper's calls for new peace talks with the guerrillas to end Colombia's three-decade-old internal conflict. He advocated ploughing more troops and more equipment into a counterinsurgency campaign to militarily defeat the rebels.
